summary: Players collect colored train cards and claim routes across a map of Europe, trying to complete ticket contracts connecting distant cities while blocking opponents on contested routes. The tunnel, ferry, and station mechanics add a bit more texture than the original US version, and the tight, often congested map creates real tension in the endgame.
praised: Easy to teach, plays in under an hour
Tunnels, ferries, and stations add welcome variety over the original game
Satisfying push-your-luck tension in deciding when to commit to routes
Good gateway game that scales well from casual to competitive groups
criticised: Luck of the ticket draw can swing outcomes significantly
Limited player interaction beyond route blocking
Can feel a bit solitaire-ish until the map gets contested
Little strategic depth for heavier gamers after repeated plays

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial over shared routes

scoring.why: Points come from route length, completed (or failed) ticket contracts, and a longest-route bonus, but ticket completion dominates the outcome
